title: Augmented ordered localization model of the Godement ring complex
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subset A$ a finitely generated ideal. Assume the ordinary derived category $D(A)$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] in the indicated universe. The actual augmented Godement mapping fibre $(K(A,I),\epsilon_{A,I})$ of [def-weil-pbc-ring-complex-godement-construction] satisfies $\operatorname{RingComplexHasCechModel}(A,I,K(A,I),\epsilon_{A,I})$ of [def-weil-pbc-ring-complex-cech-data]. Thus every finite generating list, including the empty list, gives the precise ordered product-localization coordinates, alternating differential, negative-degree vanishing and degree-zero identity augmentation, together with an augmentation-compatible isomorphism to $K(A,I)$ in $D(A)$.

proof.text: For each generating list construct the actual principal cover and its ordered Cech restriction fibre. The coordinate theorem supplies all localization coordinates, differential formulas, negative vanishing and the degree-zero projection equation for this fixed fibre.

The specified Godement augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism and nonnegative; its terms identify with iterated products of stalk skyscrapers and are flasque. The affine-section theorem supplies the section augmentation quasi-isomorphisms. Apply finiteOrderedFlasqueCechComparison to obtain the two quasi-isomorphisms to the ordered double total and their degree-zero augmentation equation.

Restriction of scalars is exact. The constant one-point ring-site functor preserves homology, as its faithful evaluation recovers the identity and reflects exactness. Apply these functors to the roof. Equality in degree zero gives equality of the two maps from A[0]. The induced cone maps are quasi-isomorphisms by the two-out-of-three theorem for distinguished triangles after localization, and shifting preserves this property. Inverse rotation gives the projection square. Invert the Godement-side map, compose the roof isomorphisms and retain the augmentation equation. Combine this isomorphism with the fixed fibre coordinates to prove the unchanged predicate.
